_comment: Defaults, committed. Put anything account-specific in config.local.json
beside this file -- it is gitignored and shallow-merged over these values,
so your username never lands in a commit. Command-line flags win over both.

_host: The address you would type into the client -- megaskywars.com, not the
machine behind it. Leaving the port at 25565 means 'no port given', and
then _minecraft._tcp.<host> is resolved first, exactly as a client does.
Most server domains have only that SRV record and no A record at all.
_username: The Microsoft account email. It is only a cache key -- the first run
prints a device code to sign in with, and the token is cached under
_auth: There is no auth setting. This proxy signs in to a real account, always;
the offline mode that would let it join without one is not exposed here.
_ranked: The ranked queue requires ViaVersion protocol 47, which a real 1.8.9
client is; casual has no version check either way. Do not bump this.

_pingIntervalMs: A ping is nine bytes, so four a second costs nothing and buys two
things: a console RTT readout that reacts at the speed a fight does,
and a congestion signal the translators can steer on. Once a second
was too coarse to be either.
_congestedRttMs: Above this round trip the console is behind, and the entity and block
streams stop queueing state until it recovers. The Broadband Adapter
drains ~10-15 KB/s and node reports no backpressure until the OS send
buffer is full, so the round trip is the only honest measure of the
queue. Raise it and the link buffers more; lower it and it sends less.

_mapMatchRadius: Maps sit >= 1800 blocks apart, so anything this side of a few hundred
blocks from an origin is unambiguously that map. Beyond every origin is
the hub, which is GCLINK_GAME_LOBBY and has no geometry we can show.
_maxBlocksPerFrame: Join-time chunk diffs run to tens of thousands of blocks. The console
re-meshes a bounded number of chunks per frame (T24), so pace the deltas
rather than handing TCP a megabyte and hoping. This is a ceiling, not a
target: the flush also stops the moment gclink.congested goes true, which
is what actually keeps a join diff from burying a fight.

entities._cap: 16 players + arrows + snowballs + a 192-stone death drop overflows 64.
_minMoveDelta: Blocks. 0.03 rounds to one unit of the wire's 1/32 fixed point, which is
no filter at all -- every entity that twitches costs 18 bytes a tick.
Both this and minTurn (in byte turns, 256 to the circle) are doubled
beyond 32 blocks and doubled again beyond 64.
